message.content:
I don’t have direct access to your network connection, so I can’t measure your current download/upload speeds myself. However, you can quickly find out what your Internet speed is by running a speed test yourself. Here’s how:

### 1. Use an Online Speed Test (Web Browser)
- **Speedtest by Ookla** – Visit https://www.speedtest.net/ and click “Go” to get a quick readout of your download, upload, and ping times.
- **Fast.com** – Go to https://fast.com/, which automatically starts measuring your download speed.

These sites will give you a snapshot of your current bandwidth at the moment you run the test.

### 2. Run a Speed Test from the Command Line
If you prefer a terminal-based approach, you can install `speedtest-cli` (Python) or use a native Windows utility.

#### On Windows (PowerShell)
```powershell
# Install the PowerShell module
Install-Module -Name Posh-SpeedTest -Scope CurrentUser

# Run the test
Invoke-SpeedTest
```

#### Using `speedtest-cli` (Python)
```bash
pip install speedtest-cli
speedtest-cli --simple
```

This prints:
```
Host: <ISP server>
Ping: <ms>
Download: <Mbps>
Upload: <Mbps>
```

### 3. Check Your Router’s Status Page
Most home routers expose a status page (often at http://192.168.0.1 or http://192.168.1.1). Log in with your admin credentials; many firmware versions display real‑time throughput statistics.

---

**Tip:** If you’re troubleshooting slow speeds, try:
- Running tests at different times of day to see if congestion is the issue.
- Connecting via Ethernet instead of Wi‑Fi to rule out wireless interference.
- Restarting your modem/router to refresh the connection.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the results or diagnosing specific issues!
